clue.text: Operatic chivalry

parts.note: the Italian word for chivalry opens the title of Mascagni's one-act opera, the rustic one

explanation.walkthrough: Mascagni's opera is Cavalleria Rusticana, 'rustic chivalry'; the first word alone is Italian for chivalry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian noun for knightly conduct heads the title of Mascagni's opera about Sicilian villagers.

clue.text: Unhappy land of Huxley

parts.note: Aldous Huxley wrote a poem whose Latin title means unhappy (infelix) followed by a land's name

explanation.surface: A gloomy country described by a novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: Aldous Huxley's poem 'Arabia Infelix' names the land; 'infelix' is Latin for unhappy, the old name for Yemen being Arabia Felix, happy Arabia.
explanation.definitionFit: Huxley titled a poem after this peninsula with the Latin tag for unhappy, inverting the classical 'Felix'.

clue.text: First male Jarrow scholar was a carpenter

parts.note: in Genesis Adam is the first man
the Venerable Bede was a monk-scholar at the monastery of Jarrow

explanation.surface: An early English monk from Jarrow is said to have worked with wood.
explanation.walkthrough: George Eliot's hero Adam Bede is a village carpenter; the two names come from Genesis and from the Venerable Bede, the Northumbrian historian.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot's title character works as a carpenter and joiner in a Midlands village.

clue.text: Some convoluted ways of Borges

parts.note: mazes are twisting paths, and a famous English collection of Borges's stories bears that title

explanation.surface: The Argentine writer's tortuous methods.
explanation.walkthrough: Labyrinths is the 1962 English selection of Borges's fiction and essays, and mazes are convoluted ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Mazes are winding passages, and the word titles a celebrated Borges collection in English.

clue.text: Greek archons offer cattle farms

indicators.note: something that is Greek to us is unintelligible, so the following word is scrambled

parts.note: archons were chief magistrates of ancient Athens

explanation.surface: Ancient Athenian magistrates provide ranches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek' looks like a description of the archons, who were indeed Greek, but it signals that ARCHONS is jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish-American word for ranches, large farms where cattle are raised.

clue.text: Smart type dispatched by 24

definitions.meaning: Hardy's heroine at 24 stabs her seducer d'Urberville

explanation.surface: A clever fellow is killed by Hardy's heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is TESS: Tess of the d'Urbervilles kills Alec d'Urberville.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart alec is a cocky know-all, and Hardy's seducer Alec d'Urberville is murdered by the heroine.

clue.text: A degree in Aryan version of Sanskrit poem

indicators.note: the article and degree are placed inside the rearranged word
a version of a word is a variant form of it, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A rendering of an ancient Indian epic includes a qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' rearranges ARYAN as RYANA, and 'in' puts A plus MA inside it after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hindu epic of Rama, composed in Sanskrit verse and attributed to Valmiki.

clue.text: High flyer with lightweight surname

parts.note: John Braine's ambitious hero of Room at the Top has a family name made of a light and a weight

explanation.surface: An ambitious man whose family name sounds trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: John Braine's Room at the Top follows a social climber; his surname splits as LAMP (a light) and TON (a weight).
explanation.definitionFit: Braine's protagonist climbs ruthlessly towards wealth, and his surname combines a lamp with a ton.

clue.text: Smooth change at loge

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters that follow

explanation.surface: Moving seats at the theatre box goes without a hitch.
explanation.walkthrough: A loge is a theatre box; 'change' rearranges AT LOGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction for playing notes smoothly joined, without breaks.

clue.text: Dorothea defied his will

parts.note: in Middlemarch Dorothea's elderly scholar husband leaves a codicil forbidding her to marry Ladislaw, which she ignores

explanation.surface: A wife resists her husband's wishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will' is both his wishes and his testament: the codicil to Edward Casaubon's will disinherits Dorothea if she marries Will Ladislaw, and she does.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot's pedantic clergyman in Middlemarch, whose testament Dorothea Brooke disregards to marry Ladislaw.

clue.text: End of bird at poet's party

definitions.meaning: the rear plumage of a rooster
T. S. Eliot's verse play is The ___ Party

explanation.surface: A rooster's rear end turns up at a literary gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: T. S. Eliot wrote the verse drama The Cocktail Party; a cock's tail is the end of a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster's tail feathers, and the mixed-drink gathering in Eliot's 1949 verse drama.

clue.text: Household word for one seen as rogue

definitions.text: Household word for one seen as rogue

parts.words: Household word for one seen as rogue
parts.note: Geoffrey Household wrote the thriller Rogue ___, about a hunted English gentleman

explanation.surface: A familiar term for someone thought a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Household' is not domestic but the novelist Geoffrey Household, whose 1939 thriller is Rogue Male; a rogue elephant is a lone male.
explanation.definitionFit: Household's title pairs rogue with this word for a man, the sex of a solitary rogue beast.

clue.text: He wrote the kind of poetry he wanted

definitions.text: He wrote the kind of poetry he wanted

parts.words: He wrote the kind of poetry he wanted
parts.note: a Scottish modernist poet wrote a long poem titled The Kind of Poetry I Want

explanation.surface: A poet composed verse exactly to his own taste.
explanation.walkthrough: Hugh MacDiarmid, the Scottish poet, published 'The Kind of Poetry I Want' (1961).
explanation.definitionFit: The pen name of C. M. Grieve, whose long poem is titled The Kind of Poetry I Want.

clue.text: Destroying the image of Byzantium

parts.note: the eighth- and ninth-century Byzantine controversy in which religious pictures were smashed

explanation.surface: Ruining the reputation of the Eastern Empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'image' looks like reputation, but means a religious icon: Byzantine emperors ordered icons destroyed.
explanation.definitionFit: The breaking of sacred pictures, a policy of Byzantine emperors in the eighth and ninth centuries.

clue.text: Possibly rid Antonio of admission to the ministry

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be rearranged into another word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Perhaps the church could free Antonio of his entry into the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges RID ANTONIO.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremony by which a person is made a priest or minister.

clue.text: French rib allowed inside to meet writer

indicators.note: the word for allowed goes within the French word

parts.note: côte is French for rib
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A French cut of meat is permitted for an author to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: COTE (French côte, rib) takes LET inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The French novelist Sidonie-Gabrielle Colette, author of Gigi and the Claudine books.

clue.text: The so-called system of — which was employed by Russell and Whitehead " (A.J. Ayer)

definitions.text: The so-called system of — which was employed by Russell and Whitehead " (A.J. Ayer)

parts.words: The so-called system of — which was employed by Russell and Whitehead " (A.J. Ayer)
parts.note: a quotation from Ayer with a gap for the old name of symbolic logic used in Principia Mathematica

explanation.surface: A philosopher's sentence about the formal method of two logicians.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank is filled from Ayer's sentence; 'logistic' was an early name for symbolic or mathematical logic.
explanation.definitionFit: An older name for symbolic logic, the formal calculus used in Principia Mathematica.

clue.text: Unyielding French sculptor with worker

parts.note: Lambert-Sigisbert Adam was an eighteenth-century French sculptor
a worker ant is the standard crossword ant

explanation.surface: A stubborn French sculptor alongside a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Adam family of Nancy were French sculptors; 'worker' is the usual ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusing to be persuaded, firm as hard stone.

clue.text: A lot of bull in one of 4

definitions.text: A lot of bull in one of 4

parts.words: A lot of bull in one of 4
parts.note: a half-bull monster lived in the Cretan maze, and 4 is a collection of mazes

explanation.surface: Plenty of nonsense in a book of Borges's stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 is LABYRINTHS; the Cretan labyrinth housed the half-bull monster, who also figures in Borges's 'The House of Asterion'.
explanation.definitionFit: The bull-headed monster of Greek myth, kept by Minos in the Cretan labyrinth.

clue.text: Outstanding art form

parts.note: outstanding here means literally standing out, projecting from a flat surface, as carved work does

explanation.surface: An excellent kind of art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' seems to praise, but means projecting: relief sculpture stands out from its background.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian term for relief sculpture, in which figures project from the background.

clue.text: Why do ye strive to bar wished death from his so just "(Phineas Fletcher, Elisa)

definitions.text: Why do ye strive to bar wished death from his so just "(Phineas Fletcher, Elisa)

parts.words: Why do ye strive to bar wished death from his so just "(Phineas Fletcher, Elisa)
parts.note: a quotation from Phineas Fletcher's elegy with a word missing, meaning entry or going in

explanation.surface: A line from a seventeenth-century elegy asking why death is kept out.
explanation.walkthrough: A quotation clue: the missing word is from Phineas Fletcher's Elisa, meaning a going in, an entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: An entering or going in, the act of entrance that death is barred from in the verse.

clue.text: Obscure time for Koestler

parts.note: Arthur Koestler's novel about Soviet show trials is Darkness at ___

explanation.surface: An unclear hour for a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Koestler's Darkness at Noon: 'obscure' means dark, so it is a dark midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday, made dark in the title of Koestler's novel of the Stalinist purges.

clue.text: Those of the midden will madden said Auden

definitions.text: Those of the midden will madden said Auden

parts.words: Those of the midden will madden said Auden
parts.note: Auden wrote that the smells of a dunghill would madden

explanation.surface: A poet remarks that a rubbish heap is infuriating.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue paraphrases an Auden line on the smells of a dunghill; a midden is a refuse heap.
explanation.definitionFit: Smells, the stinks rising from a midden or dunghill.

clue.text: Poet in terrible riot about 24 being sent back

indicators.note: the scrambled word goes around the reversed name
terrible signals that the letters of the next word are in disarray
sent back means the name is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the answer to 24 is Hardy's heroine

explanation.surface: A poet caught in a dreadful disturbance about Hardy's heroine being returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges RIOT as ROTI; 'being sent back' turns TESS into SSET; 'about' wraps ROTI round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Christina or Dante Gabriel, the Pre-Raphaelite family of poets.

clue.text: She was also called Clare

parts.note: Hardy's heroine marries Angel Clare and so takes his surname

explanation.surface: A woman had another name.
explanation.walkthrough: Tess Durbeyfield marries Angel Clare in Hardy's novel, becoming Mrs Clare.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardy's heroine, Tess Durbeyfield, bears her husband Angel's surname after their wedding.

clue.text: Insured a different name once given to the Po?

definitions.text: name once given to the Po?

indicators.note: a different form of the words means their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A guaranteed policy carries another label for an Italian river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges INSURED with A; the question mark marks the Po as one identification of a mythical river.
explanation.definitionFit: The river of Greek myth into which Phaethon fell, identified in antiquity with the Italian Po.

clue.text: Manners of speaking from identity of mythical princess on manuscript

parts.note: ID is short for identity
Io was an Argive princess loved by Zeus and turned into a heifer

explanation.surface: Ways of talking derived from a Greek princess's papers.
explanation.walkthrough: Io is the princess of Greek myth; 'on' simply joins the last piece after the first two.
explanation.definitionFit: Set expressions peculiar to a language, its characteristic turns of phrase.

clue.text: Dean's remark initially modified

parts.note: an Oxford don gave his name to slips in which the starting sounds of words are swapped

explanation.surface: A cleric's comment changed at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: William Spooner, Warden of New College, was earlier its dean; his slips swap the initial sounds of words, so they are 'initially modified'.
explanation.definitionFit: A verbal slip transposing the first sounds of two words, named after the Oxford don W. A. Spooner.
